value.text: dd-core landed as a pure library: parse, address grammar, the validate engine with configurable depth, and derived state — all structured failures, no envelope vocabulary, no filesystem.

Schema resolution proven against a fake-fs corpus that plants the same qualified name in every root: first hit wins in doc-folder -> gitroot -> .harness -> home order, and each shadowed duplicate is reported with its own path rather than silently discarded. 3 files, 39 tests green.
A same-root duplicate is a hard error while a cross-root duplicate is a reported shadow. The asymmetry is deliberate: precedence answers the second case, and nothing can answer the first.

Review finding: the deep scan carried an undocumented semantic depth cap, so a package nested past it was reported as absent rather than as too deep. Fixed and given a fixture that crosses the bound — an invented limit now has a name, a ruling, and a test.

Review finding: the loud-failure fallback never fired, because the shared filesystem adapter flattened every errno to 'no entries' — an unreadable root and an empty one were indistinguishable. Fixed with a dd-owned filesystem port that keeps the errno split honest.

Suites that spawn the CLI are proven from both sanctioned invocations — from harness/cli and from the repository root — because a fix proven from one leaves the other unproven. 16 files green from each.

Custom enums land with their own gate-terminal sets, and a schema declaring two different sets for its state fields is refused at declaration time — derived state takes exactly one set, so the ambiguity is answered where it is written, not where it is read.

`dd validate` flipped live end-to-end: a good document exits ok, an ERROR-class document exits with its issue's own code, and depth 2 versus depth 3 genuinely differ on a three-hop corpus. Pointing the verb straight at a known-bad fixture still fails — sweep exclusions belong to the doctor, never to direct invocation.

The baked docs corpus ships compiled into the CLI, so an agent can read it with no checkout and no network, and a regenerate-and-diff gate fails the moment the committed module stops matching its sources. Proven both ways: clean tree exits 0, injected drift exits 1.

dd-core isolation is machine-enforced: dependency-cruiser rule sets plus an architecture test over the import graph prove core imports no envelope module, no act, and no Node adapter. The boundary survives a reviewer who forgets to look.

This corpus was authored and validated for the first time: a real plan, its phase-2 task file with one evidence list per task, a coverage survey, and this log — four documents that cite each other by address instead of by prose. The remaining half of AC-09 (byte-stable render, doctor sweep, jq demo) is recorded by the phase-5 proof run.
